figures.body_html: Every figure in Table 1-1 as the IRS printed it, in thousands of dollars. The Data Book page of this repository carries the notes, markers and hierarchy in full.

blocks.html:
Measures

  • Gross collections: taxes collected. “Gross collections include penalties and interest in addition to taxes.” (FY2024 book, note 1)
  • Refunds: “Includes overpayment refunds, refunds resulting from examination activity, refundable tax credits, and other outlays required by law.” They include interest paid on refunds, and exclude “refunds credited to taxpayer accounts for tax liability in a subsequent year” (FY2025 book, note 2). Stimulus and pandemic payments count as refunds (FY2008 book, note 4; FY2020-2022 books, note 5).
  • Net collections: gross collections less refunds. The IRS makes no refund estimate for the parts of income and OASDHI taxes, so net collections exist only for the five types of tax and the total (FY2024 book, note 4).
  • Share of total: the IRS's own printed percentage of U.S. gross or net collections. For refunds, which the IRS prints no share of, it is our figure: each type's refunds over total refunds.

Types of tax

  • Individual income taxes: income tax withheld, and payments, which “Includes collections of estimated income tax and payments made in conjunction with individual income tax return filings.” (FY2024 book, note 5). Also estate and trust income tax. The FY2008 book on prints payments and estate and trust income tax separately; earlier books print them as one line, Other.
  • Employment taxes: “Includes taxes for Old-Age, Survivors, Disability, and Hospital Insurance (OASDHI); unemployment insurance under the Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA); and railroad retirement under the Railroad Retirement Tax Act (RRTA).” (Table 1-6, FY2025 book, note 4). OASDHI is FICA, on wages, and SECA, on self-employment income. “The OASDHI tax collections and refunds shown in this table are based on estimates made by the Secretary of the Treasury” (FY2024 book, note 4).
  • Business income taxes: “Includes taxes on corporation income (Form 1120 series) and on unrelated business income from tax-exempt organizations (Form 990-T).” (Table 1-6, FY2025 book, note 2). Partnerships, S corporations, regulated investment companies, and real estate investment trusts are not shown: “these entities generally do not have a tax liability” (FY2024 book).
  • Excise taxes: “Excludes excise taxes collected by U.S. Customs and Border Protection and the Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau.” (FY2024 book, note 7)
  • Estate and gift taxes: the federal estate tax and gift tax.

Years and dollars

  • Fiscal year: October through September. “FY 1977 covered October 1976 through September 1977” (Table 1-6, FY2025 book, note 6).
  • Nominal dollars: as printed. “All money amounts are in current dollars.” (FY2024 book)
  • FY2025 dollars: our conversion with the GDP price index (FRED GDPDEF, retrieved September 29, 2026), averaged over each fiscal year.
  • “Collection and refund data may not be comparable for a given fiscal year because payments made in prior years may be refunded in the current fiscal year.” (FY2024 book)

Known problems in the source

  • FY2015 excise refunds are printed as $7,445,780 thousand. The same row's net collections, $76,457,302 thousand, is gross collections of $77,201,882 thousand less $744,580 thousand: the printed figure has an extra digit. The charts draw it as printed.
  • FY1999 OASDHI net collections, $585,974,264 thousand, are not gross less refunds ($583,607,786 thousand).

One panel per type of return, each on its own scale: individual returns are counted in the hundreds of millions, estate tax returns in the tens of thousands. The markers are changes the IRS's own notes describe:

  • FY2002: Form 5500 employee plan returns “which are now processed at the Department of Labor” (FY2002 book, note 1).
  • FY2007: the one-time telephone excise refund: “Form 1040EZ-T (Federal telephone excise tax refund return)” (FY2007 book, note 2).
  • FY2008: the 2008 stimulus payments “resulted in a temporary increase in the number of individual income tax returns filed in Fiscal Year 2008” (Table 1-4, FY2009 book, note 3).
  • FY2009: tax-exempt returns count the Form “990-N (electronic notice [e-Postcard]” (FY2009 book, note 7).
  • FY2011: forms that “have been excluded in the Fiscal Year 2011 edition” (FY2011 book).
  • FY2020: “the IRS shut down Submission Processing units across the Service” (FY2020 book).
  • FY2022: supplemental documents include the electronic Form 1040-X. No note of this table says so; the FY2022 notes of Tables 1-3 and 1-4 do (shared/config/definition_breaks.csv).

blocks.html:
Types of return

  • Individual income tax returns: “Includes the Form 1040 series as follows: 1040; 1040-NR (nonresident alien income tax return)”…” (FY2025 book, note 3). Forms 1040A and 1040EZ are printed apart through the FY2000 book.
  • S corporations: “are not strictly income tax returns because S corporations are not taxed directly” (FY2005 book, note 5), but the IRS counts them with income tax returns.
  • Supplemental documents: amended returns and extensions. “Includes Forms 1040X (amended individual income tax)”…” (FY1999 book, note 6). From FY2022 they include the electronic Form 1040-X.
  • Not counted: the table “Excludes information returns” (FY2008 book, note 1), such as Forms 1099 and W-2.

Figures

  • Change from prior year: the IRS's own figure. “Percentage changes are based on rounded data.” (FY2020 book)
  • Counts: some books print a few rows in thousands of returns. Every figure here is a count.

blocks.html:
Channels

  • By a practitioner: “Includes cases in which a taxpayer transmitted the return via an authorized e-file provider, who was, in most cases, also the return preparer” (FY2025 book, note 7).
  • Self-prepared online: “Online e-filing is an option that allows taxpayers to prepare and file tax returns using a personal computer.” (FY2025 book, note 4) Free File and Direct File are part of it.
  • TeleFile: filing by touch-tone telephone; the program “was discontinued on August 16, 2005” (FY2005 book, note 3).
  • Direct File: FY2024, “Taxpayers were eligible for Direct File if they lived in one of twelve participating states” (FY2024 book, note 6).

Our figures

  • E-file share: e-filed returns (Table 1-4) over returns filed (Table 1-3), same state, type, and year. Checked on every pairing: no state-year goes above 100%.
  • Per 1,000 residents: with the Census Bureau's July 1 population estimate (FRED series POP).

Measures

  • Employment taxes: “Includes taxes for Old-Age, Survivors, Disability, and Hospital Insurance (OASDHI); unemployment insurance under the Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA); and railroad retirement under the Railroad Retirement Tax Act (RRTA).” (FY2025 book, note 4)

Years and dollars

  • Fiscal year: “FY 1976 covered July 1975 through June 1976”, and “FY 1977 covered October 1976 through September 1977” (FY2025 book, note 6). The quarter between them is not in these figures.
  • FY2025 dollars: our conversion with the GDP price index (FRED GDPDEF, retrieved September 29, 2026), averaged over each fiscal year: July-June through FY1976, October-September from FY1977.

blocks.html:
What a refund is

  • “Includes overpayment refunds, refunds resulting from examination activity, refundable tax credits, and other refunds required by law.” (FY2021 book, note 1)
  • Economic impact payments: the pandemic laws “included provisions to distribute economic impact payments to qualified taxpayers” (Table 1-7, FY2022 book, note 3).
  • Advance child tax credit: “The ARP Act included provisions to distribute monthly advance child tax credit payments to qualified taxpayers from July 2021 through December 2021.” (Table 1-7, FY2022 book, note 4)
  • Stimulus payments, FY2008-09: the Economic Stimulus Act of 2008 payments, printed in their own column.

Where a refund is counted

  • By the filer's address. “Sole proprietors, partners in a partnership, or shareholders in an S corporation may use their business addresses.” (Table 1-7, FY2022 book)
  • FY1995-97 are reported by IRS district. A state has a figure where its district was the whole state, or where the book printed a memo total for the state; the rest are grey.

Our figures

  • Less stimulus and advance payments: the printed figure less the IRS's own payment columns.
  • Per resident: with the Census Bureau's July 1 population estimate (FRED series POP).

  • “Includes overpayment refunds, refunds resulting from examination activity, refundable tax credits, and other outlays required by law.” “Also includes $16.8 billion in interest”… (FY2025 book, note 1)
  • Economic impact payments: the pandemic laws “included provisions to distribute economic impact payments to qualified taxpayers” (Table 1-7, FY2022 book, note 3).
  • Advance child tax credit: “The ARP Act included provisions to distribute monthly advance child tax credit payments to qualified taxpayers from July 2021 through December 2021.” (Table 1-7, FY2022 book, note 4)
  • Stimulus payments, FY2008-09: the Economic Stimulus Act of 2008 payments, printed in their own column.

Where a refund is counted

  • By the filer's address. “Sole proprietors, partners in a partnership, or shareholders in an S corporation may use their business addresses.” (Table 1-7, FY2022 book)
  • FY1995-97 are reported by IRS district. A state has a figure where its district was the whole state, or where the book printed a memo total for the state; the rest are grey.

Our figures

  • Less stimulus and advance payments: the printed figure less the IRS's own payment columns.
  • Average refund: this table over Table 1-7, same state, type, and year.
  • Per resident: with the Census Bureau's July 1 population estimate (FRED series POP).
